notes: SHIP v1.14.406 - NO SILENT FAILURES: TWO P0 STORAGE DEFECTS AND THE FALSE CRASH BANNER. Three defects, all found by the new automated regression baseline (test/e2e, 104 tests) rather than in the field, and all three of the same family: the app knew something and did not tell the operator. Owner-directed. P0-1, THE MASTER SAVE WAS INVISIBLE ON FAILURE. PHANTOM_MASTER_STORE.save wrote through a raw localStorage.setItem whose quota branch did a console.warn and returned false with no toast and no haptic, and its single caller discarded the boolean. On a full device the operator loaded a Master, the parse succeeded, the UI reported success, and NOTHING PERSISTED - silently gone at the next cold start. This is the largest payload in the app and the one most likely to hit quota: a 4000-host site compresses to roughly 6.5MB against a roughly 5MB Safari origin quota, which the stress harness already reproduces. Both failure branches now toast, fire the standard triple haptic and raise window.__phantomStorageFull, and the caller records a false return. The message is deliberately capability-specific rather than routed through safeStore's generic Storage full, because the thing a tech actually needs to know is that the Master still works for THIS session and must be re-imported after a restart - a generic quota toast does not say that. P0-2, SHIFT END SWALLOWED EVERYTHING. shift_end_write was a raw setItem inside a bare try catch with an empty handler: on quota it stored nothing, threw nothing, warned nothing and toasted nothing, while the hero went on rendering a countdown that would not survive the next launch. phantom_shift_end is registry-classified USER DATA, not ephemeral UI state. It now writes through safeStore, which already owns the quota toast, the haptic and the storage-full flag, so the fix REMOVES the hand-written swallow rather than adding a second handler, and returns the outcome instead of discarding it. P1, THE INSTRUMENT REPORTED A CRASH ON EVERY SUCCESS. .403's aisle_trace routes fourteen NORMAL lifecycle events through phantom_logErr, which appends to the crash ring AND force-shows the shared #crash-banner reading JS ERROR - tap to view crash log. A perfectly healthy Open Aisle therefore raised a JS-ERROR banner over the technician's screen and left it there. This mattered immediately: the consolidated device pass for the open batch runs against this build, and every tester would have reported a crash that never happened. phantom_logErr takes an optional third argument, opts.trace, which stores type trace and never raises the banner; the parameter is optional and defaults to the previous behaviour so all 64 existing call sites are byte-identical. ONE new predicate, phantom_crashErrors, is the single definition of is this ring entry an error, consumed by the three surfaces that ask it - the banner in phantom_logErr, the boot banner in phantomDeferredInit and the SYS header count in errors_refreshCount - because a second copy is exactly how they would drift apart. The ERRORS sheet is deliberately NOT filtered: listing the traces is the entire point of the .403 instrument, and they now render honestly as TRACE rather than as CAUGHT. LEGACY - READ THIS, IT IS NOT A BYTE-IDENTICAL SHIP AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Three of these changes are reachable under ?legacy=1 and none of them is gated, on the .402 precedent: only the PRESENTATION is house-scoped, the INVARIANT never is. No-silent-failures is an invariant, and legacy is entitled to not lose an operator's Master in silence. (1) The Master-save toast and the shift-end quota toast now fire in BOTH houses where legacy was previously silent. That is the fix, not a leak - a legacy user losing their Master with no indication is the same defect, and gating the honesty to redesign would be preserving a data-loss bug for the sake of the rule. (2) The boot crash banner is NOT redesign-gated, so before this fix one aisle open left fourteen trace entries in the ring and the NEXT cold boot opened with JS ERROR in BOTH houses; filtering traces RESTORES what ?legacy=1 did before .403 introduced trace entries into a ring that had only ever held faults - it moves legacy back toward its pre-.403 behaviour, not away from it. The banner mutation inside phantom_logErr stays redesign_isOn()-gated exactly as it was, and the SYS header count is only ever invoked under rd, so neither of those touches legacy at all. Nothing in the legacy markup, the legacy render paths, showPage/showOpsTab or #ops-tab-strip is modified. NOT DONE, deliberately and reported rather than absorbed: shift_end_clear still uses a raw removeItem with a bare catch (a failed delete is not data loss, and safeRemove exists if the owner wants it); phantom_logErr's own ring write is still a raw setItem (diagnostics, not user data); aisle traces still emit a console.warn labelled phantom_logErr (console noise, not the aisle); and the nine-cell OPS wall reachability regression, the four dead SOP and Rack Map doors, the history defect that drops a tech out of the app on back, the 27px header pill and the 2.75:1 nav labels are all recorded in the baseline and untouched here - one ship, one subject. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4557/4557 delta 0, CRLF intact with zero lone LF, PRECACHE untouched, three-stamp lockstep, diff is one file plus the two stamps. PROOF: the three regression tests that pinned these defects at .405 all flipped to expected to fail but passed, and their test.fail annotations are now removed so any regression fails loudly. DEVICE-VERIFY, folded into the open batch pass rather than adding a pass of its own: clear the service-worker cache, confirm the app reports v1.14.406, open Build and tap OPEN AISLE and confirm NO JS ERROR banner appears on a healthy open, confirm SYS then ERRORS still lists the AISLE trace entries and now labels them TRACE, confirm the header error count reads NONE while only traces are present, and confirm ?legacy=1 opens with no JS ERROR banner after an aisle visit.
